one_liner: Rust image-processing engine (CLI plus C-ABI library) for server-side decode, linear-light resize and encode; pitched against ImageMagick.
what_it_does: Imageflow runs whole image jobs (decode, crop/resize/composite, re-encode with mozjpeg, libpng/pngquant, libwebp or the newer pure-Rust 'zen' codecs) described either as ImageResizer-style querystrings (`width=200&height=200&mode=max`) or as JSON operation graphs. It ships as `imageflow_tool` (CLI), `libimageflow` (shared library with a stable C ABI and headers in bindings/headers) and bindings for .NET, Node, Go and others. It is not a drop-in for ImageMagick's command line or MagickCore API.
how_it_is_fast: For JPEG it pre-shrinks during decode: the ir4 layer asks the decoder to downscale to about 2.1x the target (decoder.min_precise_scaling_ratio default 2.1), and c_components/lib/codecs_jpeg_idct_fast.c replaces libjpeg's IDCT with 8x8 blocks reduced to NxN in linear light through sRGB/linear lookup tables. The remaining resize is a separable two-pass filter (Robidoux by default for downscaling) in linear float, now delegated to the zenresize crate's streaming API. The published benchmarks get throughput by running one imageflow_tool process per image under GNU parallel; the newer zenjpeg decode path can also split one decode across a Rayon pool (benchmarks/c-vs-zen-codecs-2026-04-15.meta.md).
when_to_use: Server-side thumbnailing or responsive-image pipelines (many JPEGs downscaled by large factors) where you want decode, linear-light resize, sharpening and an optimizing encoder in one call.
Replacing ImageResizer or an ImageMagick-based thumbnailer behind an HTTP API, using the querystring syntax or Imageflow.Server.
C or C++ services that can link a shared library through a small, stable C ABI (create context, add buffers, send JSON, read output) instead of embedding ImageMagick.
AGPL-compatible projects, or teams willing to buy the commercial licence.
when_not_to_use: Closed-source or SaaS products that cannot meet AGPL-3.0 and will not buy a commercial licence.

When you need a standalone resize kernel on raw pixel buffers: fast_image_resize or libvips are lighter, and the FastResize harness measured imageflow 2.0 slower than libvips on JPEG (6.60 s vs 5.24 s).
When you need ImageMagick's breadth (hundreds of formats, drawing, effects, scripting): Imageflow covers web formats and resize/crop/composite operations.

When you need byte-for-byte comparable output to an sRGB-space resizer: defaults scale in linear light and pre-shrink JPEGs in the IDCT, so results differ unless you set down.colorspace=srgb and decoder.min_precise_scaling_ratio.
When you need a stable Rust API: only the C ABI is versioned, `imageflow_core` is not semver-stable, and the CHANGELOG queues breaking changes for the codec/engine rewrite.

integration.form: shared lib (libimageflow, C ABI) or CLI (imageflow_tool); Rust crates are not semver-stable
integration.dependencies: default c-codecs build bundles mozjpeg-sys (nasm), libpng-sys, libwebp-sys, lcms2, libz-sys plus local C SIMD shims; optional zen-codecs feature is pure Rust (zenjpeg, zenpng, zenwebp, zengif, zenavif, mozjpeg-rs); resizing via zenresize
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.93 (rust-version declared by all workspace crates, checked by the CI msrv job); nasm for the C JPEG codec
integration.platforms: prebuilt binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux (glibc; .deb for amd64 and arm64); Docker images for Linux
integration.thread_safety: Per the C header, since ABI 3.1 a context may be used from several threads with internal serialization; use one context per thread for throughput

gotchas: Quote querystring commands in shells: an unquoted `&` backgrounds the process and drops every key after the first. The project's own 2020 benchmark (docker/imageflow_bench_ubuntu20/bench.sh) has this bug.
Linear-light scaling and IDCT pre-shrink are on by default; `down.colorspace=srgb` switches both off (and enables WebP decoder scaling hints instead).

In imageflow_riapi/src/ir4/mod.rs `get_preshrink_ratio` computes the height ratio as `from.h / to.w` (target width, not height). For landscape targets this underestimates the downscale ratio, so JPEG pre-shrink is less aggressive than documented, and for 5104x3380 to 2000 px it is skipped entirely. This costs speed, not output quality.
AGPL-3.0 also covers in-process use of libimageflow in network services; the commercial licence is sold through imageresizing.net.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over libvips when you want a single licensed, job-level API (querystring/JSON, built-in mozjpeg/pngquant encoding, ImageResizer compatibility) more than raw speed, since no valid measurement shows it beating libvips today. Pick MagicScaler instead for a .NET-native linear-light pipeline, and fast_image_resize or Pillow-SIMD when you only need the resize kernel.
verified_claims_summary: The README's 'up to 17x faster than ImageMagick' comes from a 2016 first-party run: the prototype flow-proto1 0.0.1 (commit f05efb8, wrappers/server/bench.sh), 32 copies of a 5104x3380 JPEG to 200x200 through GNU parallel under perf stat on a Xeon E3-1275 v5. It took 0.928 s against 15.837 s for ImageMagick 6.9.3-7 Q16 HDRI/OpenMP (about 17x, derived) and 3.055 s for libvips 8.3.1 (gist raw output). The catalogued 2020 hyperfine table (imageflow_tool v1.4.0-rc40 built with TARGET_CPU=haswell; Ubuntu 20.04 ImageMagick and libvips; machine not stated) gives 373.9 ms vs 6555.1 ms and 1002.8 ms. Those Imageflow rows do not time the resize, because the unquoted `&` in the parallel command backgrounds imageflow_tool.
status_note: Actively developed (last commit 2026-08-29 per the verifier; the imazen org listing shows the repo updated 2026-09-28; 4.4k stars) but still labelled release candidate and mid-migration to pure-Rust codecs and a new engine; dual-licensed AGPL-3.0 or commercial.
measurement_notes: Measurement flaw that invalidates the catalogued 2020 Imageflow rows (373.9 ms at 200x200 and 1.014 s at 2000x2000; ratios 17.53x vs ImageMagick and 2.68x vs libvips). The benchmark page source (imazen/imageflow-web _pages/benchmarks.md) and docker/imageflow_bench_ubuntu20/bench.sh pass imageflow_tool to GNU parallel as `parallel "$HOME/bin/imageflow_tool v1/querystring --in {} ... --command width=200&height=200&mode=max&quality=100" ::: *.jpg` (the website shows a `v0.1/ir4 ... width=200&height=200&quality=90` variant with the same numbers). The ampersands are protected from hyperfine's shell by the double quotes but reach the shell that GNU parallel spawns per job unquoted. That shell runs `imageflow_tool ... --command width=200` in the background, treats height=200, mode=max and quality=100 as variable assignments, and exits at once. GNU parallel's default --group mode buffers job output in temporary files, so it does not wait for the orphaned child, and hyperfine stops its clock when parallel exits. I reproduced this in a scratch directory with GNU parallel 20150329 (Ubuntu 20.04 ships 20161222, not tested) and a stand-in tool that sleeps 2 s: with the bench.sh quoting, parallel returned after 0.27 s and the tool received only `--command width=200`; with the value quoted, parallel waited 2.1 s and the tool got the full command. So the Imageflow column times shell and job launch (the 0.27 s Perl startup plus about 3 ms per job is close to 373.9 ms) plus contention from earlier runs' background jobs, not the resize. The libvips and ImageMagick rows contain no `&` and are timed to completion. Suggest rejecting the 2020 numbers as invalid evidence (precedent: MQF timed a no-op). The README's '17x' derives from the 2016 run, which has no `&` problem: flow-proto1 0.0.1 at commit f05efb8, perf stat, Xeon E3-1275 v5; gist: 0.928 s, 6290 ms task-clock vs ImageMagick 6.9.3-7 Q16 HDRI OpenMP 15.837 s, 120853 ms task-clock (about 17x wall, 19x CPU, derived) and libvips 8.3.1 3.055 s. But it measured a prototype, not imageflow_tool: in issue #132 (May 2017) a user measured imageflow_tool at 135.24 s vs flow-proto1 17.12 s and vipsthumbnail 97.09 s. It is also first-party and not like-for-like. libvips was run with --linear, which disables JPEG shrink-on-load (libvips 8.9.1 thumbnail.c: 'We can't use pre-shrunk images in linear mode'). ImageMagick got no -define jpeg:size hint, while Imageflow pre-shrinks JPEGs in the IDCT by default (ir4 min_precise_scaling_ratio 2.1). ImageMagick's OpenMP threads were not limited (no MAGICK_THREAD_LIMIT) while GNU parallel ran one convert per core. Tier stays C at best for the README claim; the 2020 table should not be used. Minor code bug: ir4 get_preshrink_ratio divides source height by target width (`from.h / to.w`). It makes pre-shrink more conservative for landscape targets and disables it for the 2000 px case, so it is not behind inflated numbers. Language override still recommended: 'Rust with a C ABI (libimageflow; bundles C components)'.
